title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
notes: Eight-lecture build-everything path (micrograd, makemore 1-5, GPT, GPT tokenizer), page marked 'ongoing'. Use as the spine for 12-17 sequencing; page is undated (year = first lecture, not confirmed on page).

title: micrograd: a tiny scalar-valued autograd engine
notes: Roughly 100-line reverse-mode engine plus a 50-line NN library. Reference shape for the module-12 browser build; learner code must be written independently.

title: nanoGPT
notes: Classic minimal GPT training repo; README now (Nov 2025) marks it deprecated in favour of nanochat. Cite only for history.

title: nanochat: The best ChatGPT that $100 can buy
notes: Single-node full pipeline (BPE tokenizer, pretraining, SFT, RL, CORE/bits-per-byte eval, KV-cache inference, tool use); GPT-2-grade model in about 2-3 h on 8xH100 per its 2026 leaderboard, plus a CPU/MPS toy script. Best local/rented-GPU capstone for 16-18.

title: minbpe: minimal byte-level BPE
notes: Minimal byte-level BPE trainer/encoder/decoder used as the tokenizer-lecture exercise. Model for the module-17 tokenizer build and its round-trip tests.

title: autoresearch: AI agents running research on single-GPU nanochat training
notes: March 2026 repo where an agent edits training code, runs 5-minute trainings, keeps or discards changes by metric, and repeats; the human edits the agents' Markdown instructions. Concrete example of agentic experiment loops for the AI-native sections.

title: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
notes: Practitioner checklist: know the data, build a skeleton with dumb baselines, overfit, regularize, tune, squeeze. Backbone of the module-13 debugging lesson.

title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders (Part 1, 2022; Part 2: Deep Learning Foundations to Stable Diffusion)
notes: Top-down course: Part 1 (2022, 9 lessons) applications first; Part 2 builds a mini framework (miniai) with callbacks, activation-stat hooks, init (Glorot/LSUV), optimizers, schedulers, then DDPM/DDIM and samplers. Good model for instrumentation and for module 20.

title: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision (Spring 2026)
notes: 2026 schedule: linear classifiers, optimization, backprop, CNNs, architectures, RNN/LSTM, attention/transformers, detection, video, distributed training, SSL, VAE/GAN/diffusion. A1-A3 cover kNN to diffusion/CLIP; explicit generative-AI policy. Reference sequencing for 13 and 15.

title: CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning (Winter 2026)
notes: 2026 sequence runs word vectors, backprop, RNN LMs, transformers, pretraining (scaling/systems/data), post-training (RLHF/SFT/DPO), prompting+PEFT, agents/tool use/RAG, benchmarking, reasoning, tokenization. Shows evaluation and agents are now core NLP content.

title: CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch (Spring 2026)
notes: Five assignments: basics (tokenizer, transformer, optimizer), systems (profiling, Triton FlashAttention2, distributed), scaling (fit laws via a training API), data (Common Crawl filtering/dedup), alignment and reasoning RL (optional DPO). Assignments ship as pytest suites wired through an adapters file; the model for local test suites.

title: Dive into Deep Learning
notes: Free interactive textbook (v1.0.3 online) with chapters from linear nets through CNNs, RNNs, attention/transformers, optimization and computational performance. Use for parallel readings; authors/year not re-checked on the page this session.

title: Understanding Deep Learning
notes: Free PDF (updated 9 Feb 2026) with 68 fill-in-the-missing-code Python notebooks, mostly NumPy, so many ideas port to Pyodide. Strong figures-first explanations for optimization, init, VAEs and diffusion.

title: Deep Learning
notes: Free online classic for math depth (optimization, regularization, sequence models, autoencoders). Reference-level reading for derivations, not a sequencing model for modern LLM topics.

title: 10-414/714 Deep Learning Systems: Algorithms and Implementation (Fall 2026)
notes: Students build the 'needle' framework across HW0-HW4: autodiff, NN library abstractions, normalization/dropout, NDArray CPU/GPU backends, CNNs, RNNs, transformers; mugrade autograder. Best model for growing the module-12 engine into a tensor library.

title: PyTorch Tutorials (v2.15)
notes: Official tutorials and recipes (site shows build 2.15.0); 'Learn the Basics' path covers tensors, data, models, autograd, optimization, saving. Production reference for module 14.

title: Autograd mechanics (PyTorch 2.15 documentation)
notes: Explains how autograd records history, saved tensors, grad modes (no-grad, inference, eval), in-place correctness checks and non-determinism. Source for the 12.6 parity lesson and several misconceptions.

title: Automatic Mixed Precision package - torch.amp
notes: Current AMP reference (last updated Jul 2026) on autocast and gradient scaling for fp16/bf16. Use for the mixed-precision lesson.

title: PyTorch Profiler (recipe)
notes: Official profiling recipe (tutorials build 2.15). Starting point for the module-29 profiling lab.

title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)
notes: Book (Sept 2024) plus open code repo: text data, attention, GPT model, pretraining, classification and instruction fine-tuning, LoRA appendix; bonus folders add BPE, KV cache, MoE, Llama/Qwen/Gemma from scratch and DPO; sequel on reasoning models. Good PyTorch-level companion for 16-17.

title: Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft, August 19, 2026 release)
notes: Aug 2026 draft reorganised: Vol I covers words/tokens, n-grams, embeddings, neural nets, transformers+pretraining, post-training; Vol II has IR/RAG, agents (unwritten), RNNs/LSTMs. Evidence that textbooks now teach transformers before RNNs.

title: Hugging Face LLM Course
notes: Twelve chapters from pipeline() use and fine-tuning through datasets, tokenizers, curation, LLM fine-tuning and 'build reasoning models'. Production-library comparison for 17; Apache-2.0.

title: Hugging Face Deep Reinforcement Learning Course
notes: Units: intro, Q-learning, DQN (Atari), Optuna tuning, policy gradients, actor-critic, multi-agent, PPO (incl. Doom). Hands-on library-first complement to Sutton & Barto; year not confirmed on page.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd ed.)
notes: Canonical RL text, free PDF; bandits to policy gradients. Spine for the tabular half of module 23.

title: Spinning Up in Deep RL

title: CS 185/285: Deep Reinforcement Learning (Spring 2026)
notes: 2026 homeworks: imitation learning, policy gradients, Q-learning and actor-critic, LLM RL, offline RL; lectures include control as inference, model-based and offline RL. Confirms LLM RL is now standard RL-course content.

title: Reinforcement Learning lectures (UCL Advanced Topics 2015)
notes: Ten classic lectures (MDPs, DP, model-free prediction/control, function approximation, policy gradients, planning, exploration, games) plus the Easy21 assignment; CC-BY-NC 4.0.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.)

notes: Forty-three pragmatic rules (launch heuristics first, simple pipeline, feature engineering, skew, monitoring). Use as discussion prompts in 27; publication year not shown on page.

notes: Free PDF; legitimacy, classification criteria (independence, separation, sufficiency), relative fairness, causality and practice. Primary text for module 30.

notes: Living, CC-BY-SA notes on accelerators, networking, storage, debugging, fault tolerance and training/inference operations (year = repo creation; updated through Nov 2026). Reference for module-29 reliability lessons.

notes: LBNL labeled HVAC fault data. Ideal capstone data for 22.6 given the learner's HVAC background.

notes: Single-file reference implementations. Production comparison for local 23.4/23.6.

notes: Disciplined convex programming in Python. cvxpy-base 1.8.2 with Clarabel solved a QP in Pyodide, enabling in-browser MPC.

notes: Continuous-depth models with adjoint gradients. Bridge from ResNets/adjoints to grey-box dynamics.

notes: Operator learning in Fourier space. Overview-only in 24.7.

notes: Sharding optimizer state, gradients and parameters. Memory-calculator lesson 29.4.

notes: Intra-layer tensor parallelism. Lesson 29.4.

notes: Design of PyTorch FSDP. Production comparison for 29.5.

notes: Dataset documentation questions. Used in 27.2 and 30.5.

notes: Models exploit unintended cues. Failure-mode lesson 30.1.

notes: FGSM and the linearity explanation. Lesson 30.3.

notes: Modern nets are overconfident; temperature scaling fixes much of it. Lesson 30.3.
